item.content:encoded:
The Harvard Academy Scholars Program offers an exceptional opportunity for outstanding early-career social scientists to conduct advanced research at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA. Organized by the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies, the program is designed for recent PhD recipients and advanced doctoral candidates whose research combines strong disciplinary expertise with deep knowledge of countries or regions outside the United States or Canada. Selected Academy Scholars receive a two-year, in-residence postdoctoral appointment, an annual $80,000 stipend, and $6,000 in annual research support, alongside access to Harvard’s academic environment, research resources, mentorship, seminars and interdisciplinary scholarly activities. For researchers working in the social sciences and pursuing internationally or regionally focused research, the program provides an opportunity to develop ambitious research projects while becoming part of a highly selective scholarly community at Harvard.

About the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies

The Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies was established to promote innovative social science research while deepening understanding of the experiences, institutions and practices of different regions and countries around the world.

The Academy places particular emphasis on research that combines:

  • Excellence in a social science discipline.
  • Strong regional or country expertise.
  • Knowledge of languages relevant to the research area.
  • Comparative, transnational or domestic research questions.
  • Research focused on regions outside the United States or Canada.

The Academy Scholars Program reflects the Academy’s belief that important social science research benefits from combining rigorous disciplinary training with detailed knowledge of particular countries and regions.

What Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

The Academy Scholars Program identifies and supports outstanding researchers who are at the beginning of their academic careers. The program is particularly suited to scholars whose research crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries and examines important issues through comparative, transnational or domestic perspectives. Academy Scholars are expected to demonstrate resourcefulness, initiative and originality in their research. Their work should show strong potential to become the foundation for future careers in research universities, international organizations or other institutions where advanced research and regional expertise are valued. Rather than simply providing financial support, the program creates an environment in which scholars can devote substantial time to research, develop new skills and engage with other researchers working across different disciplines and regions.

Two-Year Postdoctoral Fellowship at Harvard University

Successful candidates are appointed for a two-year, in-residence postdoctoral fellowship at the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. During the fellowship, Academy Scholars become part of an interdisciplinary research community and participate actively in the intellectual life of Harvard.

The program provides scholars with the opportunity to:

  • Conduct substantial independent research.
  • Develop ambitious research projects.
  • Strengthen research methodologies and disciplinary skills.
  • Engage with scholars from different academic backgrounds.
  • Participate in seminars and workshops.
  • Exchange ideas through academic discussions and informal gatherings.
  • Receive mentorship from Harvard Academy Senior Scholars.
  • Present research to colleagues and members of the Harvard academic community.
  • Build relationships that can support future academic and professional development.

The Academy’s environment is specifically designed to encourage scholars to approach their research from innovative and interdisciplinary perspectives.

Financial Support for Academy Scholars

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program provides substantial financial support to selected scholars. Each year, approximately five to six Academy Scholars are selected for two-year appointments.

The financial package includes:

Annual Stipend of $80,000

Each Academy Scholar receives an annual stipend of $80,000 during the appointment.

Annual Research Support of $6,000

In addition to the stipend, scholars receive $6,000 per year in research support.

This additional support is intended to help scholars pursue their research projects and meet appropriate research-related needs during their time at the Academy.

In-Residence Research Environment

The program is based at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The in-residence structure allows selected scholars to become actively involved in the Academy’s intellectual community while working on their research. The two years of the appointment must be completed within a three-year window.

Important Fellowship Terms

Applicants should carefully understand the terms associated with the appointment before applying.

Year 1 Start Requirement

The first year of the fellowship must begin no later than the fall immediately following the postdoctoral fellowship offer.

Delays or deferrals in the start of Year 1 are not permitted.

Leave Between Years 1 and 2

Between the first and second years, Academy Scholars may apply for a one-time leave of up to 12 months.

This leave may be used to:

  • Accept a tenure-track teaching appointment; or
  • Continue with a tenure-track teaching appointment.

The leave is not available for other professional reasons.

Restrictions on Outside Funding and Obligations

Academy Scholars may not accept outside funding, awards or obligations during their appointment.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider their existing and anticipated commitments before accepting the fellowship.

Potential Teaching Opportunity

Academy Scholars may be invited to teach a course at Harvard during their appointment.

This provides an additional opportunity for scholars who are interested in developing their teaching experience alongside their research.

Mentorship Through Harvard Academy Senior Scholars

One of the distinctive aspects of the Academy Scholars Program is its mentorship structure. Academy Scholars are mentored by Harvard Academy Senior Scholars, a group of faculty members who participate in the Academy’s activities and serve as the selection committee. The Senior Scholars are committed to helping Academy Scholars develop their research and reach their academic potential. This mentorship can be particularly valuable for researchers at the beginning of their academic careers because it provides opportunities to receive feedback from established scholars working across a range of disciplines and geographic areas.

An Interdisciplinary Academic Community

The Academy Scholars Program is designed around interdisciplinary exchange.

Academy Scholars meet through:

  • Dinners.
  • Seminars.
  • Informal academic gatherings.
  • Workshops.
  • Conferences.
  • Research presentations.
  • Other Harvard Academy activities.

These interactions allow researchers to discuss their work with scholars whose disciplinary backgrounds may differ from their own.

The Academy also provides opportunities for scholars to present their research to colleagues, Harvard Academy Senior Scholars, faculty members and graduate students.

The program notes that some Academy Scholars also have the opportunity to present book manuscripts for intensive discussion through Academy-sponsored authors’ conferences.

Research Focus and Regional Expertise

A central requirement of the Academy Scholars Program is that applicants demonstrate knowledge or expertise concerning countries or regions outside the United States or Canada. This means that applicants should not simply demonstrate excellence in a social science discipline. Their research should also show meaningful engagement with a specific country, group of countries or broader region outside the United States or Canada.

Relevant research may examine:

  • Political systems.
  • Economic development.
  • Social change.
  • International relations.
  • History.
  • Culture.
  • Institutions.
  • Governance.
  • Comparative societies.
  • Transnational issues.
  • Domestic issues within particular countries or regions.
  • Other significant social science questions.

The Academy is particularly interested in scholarship that can illuminate important issues through detailed regional or country-level knowledge.

Who Can Apply for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

The program is open to two primary groups:

  1. Recent recipients of PhD or equivalent degrees in the social sciences.
  2. Advanced doctoral candidates in the social sciences.

For applicants who have already received their PhD or equivalent degree, the degree must have been granted within two years of the August 1, 2027 start date. Advanced doctoral candidates may also apply if they are sufficiently close to completing their dissertation and can satisfy the program’s documentation requirements.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should carefully review the following eligibility requirements.

PhD or Equivalent Degree

Applicants who have already completed their doctoral degree must have received their PhD or equivalent degree within two years of August 1, 2027.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to researchers who are at the beginning of their postdoctoral careers.

Advanced Doctoral Candidates

Advanced doctoral candidates in the social sciences are also eligible.

However, scholars who are approaching dissertation completion must be able to provide official degree-conferral documentation issued by their university registrar by June 30, 2027, in order to begin the appointment on August 1, 2027.

Social Science Background

The program is specifically intended for researchers working in the social sciences.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate a strong disciplinary foundation in a relevant social science field and present a research project that fits the intellectual objectives of the Academy.

Regional or Country Expertise

Applicants are expected to combine social science expertise with knowledge or expertise concerning countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

Relevant language knowledge may also be important depending on the applicant’s research area and methodology.

Previous Postdoctoral Fellowship

Applicants who hold or have completed another postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible to apply.

This is an important restriction and should be checked carefully before an applicant begins preparing their application.

Nationality and Geographic Eligibility

The information provided by Harvard does not establish a specific nationality, race or continental restriction for applicants.

Therefore, the opportunity should not be presented as being limited to applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East or any other particular continent. The key geographic requirement relates to the subject of the applicant’s research and regional expertise, which should concern countries or regions outside the United States or Canada. Applicants from different countries may therefore be considered provided they meet the academic and research requirements.

What Application Materials Are Required?

Applicants must submit a complete application consisting of several important documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a CV, including a list of publications.

The CV should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s academic background, research experience, publications and other relevant scholarly achievements.

2. Research Proposal

Applicants must submit a research proposal of no more than 2,000 words.

The proposal should explain:

  • The intellectual objectives of the proposed research.
  • The research questions or problems being investigated.
  • The planned methodological approach.
  • The disciplinary work involved.
  • The significance of the proposed project.
  • How the research fits the applicant’s academic trajectory.

Applicants may include footnotes, endnotes and bibliographies where appropriate.

References are not required, but if they are included, they do not count toward the 2,000-word limit.

3. Scholarly Writing Sample

Applicants must submit one scholarly writing sample.

Examples include:

  • A chapter from a PhD dissertation.
  • A peer-reviewed journal article.
  • Another substantial piece of scholarly writing.

The writing sample must:

  • Be written in English.
  • Be no longer than 50 pages.
  • Demonstrate the applicant’s scholarly and analytical abilities.

Co-authored work is acceptable provided that each author’s contribution is clearly specified and the authorship is not shared with an academic advisor.

4. PhD Program Transcript

Applicants must provide a copy of their PhD program transcript.Applicants who studied at universities outside the United States should pay particular attention to Harvard’s requirements concerning transcript-like documentation. The Academy indicates that its reviewers consider applications from international universities and may request as much official transcript-like documentation as the applicant’s university registrar can provide for graduate-level study, including Master’s and PhD programs. Applicants should therefore contact their university registrar or relevant academic office early if they need official documentation.

5. Three Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must obtain three letters of recommendation.

These letters must be:

  • Submitted directly by the recommenders.
  • Submitted confidentially.
  • Uploaded through the online application system.

An important application detail is that applicants must submit their application before the upload link is sent to their recommenders.

Applicants should therefore plan their application timeline carefully and communicate with their recommenders well in advance.

Application Deadline

The main application deadline for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program is:

September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Harvard states that late applications are not accepted.

There is a separate deadline for recommendation letters.

Recommendation Letter Deadline

Letters of recommendation must arrive no later than:

September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

All other application materials must be submitted by September 18, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their application because recommenders need time to receive their upload links and submit their confidential letters.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted online through the Harvard Academy’s application system.

Applicants should prepare all required documents before beginning the submission process.

The application process generally involves:

  1. Preparing an up-to-date academic CV.
  2. Developing the research proposal within the 2,000-word limit.
  3. Selecting an appropriate scholarly writing sample.
  4. Obtaining the required PhD program transcript.
  5. Identifying three appropriate academic recommenders.
  6. Preparing the application and uploading the required documents as PDF files.
  7. Submitting the application before the September 18 deadline.
  8. Ensuring that all three recommenders submit their confidential letters by September 28.

Harvard states that all application materials, including recommendation letters, are submitted online as PDF documents.

Application Timeline

Applicants should be aware of the following key dates:

Stage Date
Application deadline September 18, 2026
Application deadline time 11:59 PM EDT
Recommendation letter deadline September 28, 2026
Recommendation letter deadline time 11:59 PM EDT
Expected award announcement December 2026
Fellowship start date August 1, 2027
Degree documentation deadline for scholars nearing completion June 30, 2027

The selection process begins immediately after the application period closes, and Harvard anticipates announcing the awards in December 2026.

What Makes This Harvard Fellowship Highly Competitive?

The Academy Scholars Program selects only five to six scholars each year.

This makes the program highly selective.

Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate more than academic qualifications. Their applications should communicate a compelling research agenda and show evidence of:

  • Intellectual originality.
  • Strong research potential.
  • Academic excellence.
  • Initiative.
  • Resourcefulness.
  • Regional or country expertise.
  • Strong disciplinary preparation.
  • Potential for a long-term research career.
  • Ability to contribute meaningfully to an interdisciplinary scholarly community.

Because the program is intended to support researchers at the beginning of their academic careers, applicants should clearly explain how the proposed project fits into their broader intellectual and professional development.

Click HERE to apply

Learn more about this opportunity: applicationinquiries@wcfia.harvard.edu/ https://academicpositions.harvard.edu/postings/16475

Why the Research Proposal Is Important

The research proposal is one of the most important parts of the application. With a maximum length of 2,000 words, applicants have limited space to communicate the intellectual significance and feasibility of their proposed research.

A strong proposal should make clear:

  1. What the research is about.
  2. Why the research question matters.
  3. What gap in existing scholarship the project addresses.
  4. How the applicant intends to conduct the research.
  5. What methodological and disciplinary approaches will be used.
  6. Why the applicant is particularly well positioned to conduct the research.
  7. How the project contributes to broader social science knowledge.

The proposal should also demonstrate the applicant’s regional or country expertise where relevant.

Importance of Language and Regional Knowledge

The Academy Scholars Program places considerable emphasis on combining disciplinary excellence with regional knowledge.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they have meaningful expertise in the country or region relevant to their research.

Depending on the project, this may involve knowledge of relevant languages, historical context, political institutions, cultural practices, social structures or other forms of specialized regional expertise.

This is one of the features that distinguishes the Academy Scholars Program from a general postdoctoral research position.

What Happens After Selection?

The selection process begins after the application deadline. Harvard anticipates announcing the results in December 2026. Selected scholars are then expected to begin their appointments according to the program’s requirements, with August 1, 2027 serving as the stated start date for the fellowship cycle described in the application. The first year must begin no later than the fall immediately following the fellowship offer, and delays or deferrals are not permitted.

A Research Opportunity for Future Academic and International Leaders

The Academy Scholars Program is designed for researchers whose work has the potential to become the foundation of significant academic or international careers.

The program specifically identifies scholars whose research shows promise for careers in:

  • Research universities.
  • International institutions.
  • Academic research.
  • International affairs.
  • Area studies.
  • Policy-related research environments.
  • Other institutions that value advanced social science expertise.

By bringing together researchers working on different regions and disciplinary questions, the Academy creates an environment where scholars can develop research that crosses conventional academic boundaries.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

It is a competitive postdoctoral research program of the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies that supports outstanding early-career social scientists whose research combines disciplinary excellence with expertise in countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

How long is the fellowship?

The appointment is for two years in residence.

The two years must be completed within a three-year window.

How much is the stipend?

Selected Academy Scholars receive an annual stipend of $80,000, plus $6,000 in annual research support.

How many scholars are selected?

Harvard states that approximately five to six Academy Scholars are selected each year.

Can doctoral candidates apply?

Yes. Advanced doctoral candidates in the social sciences may apply.

Those nearing dissertation completion must be able to provide degree-conferral documentation from their university registrar by June 30, 2027 for the August 1, 2027 start date.

Can someone who already completed another postdoctoral fellowship apply?

No. Individuals who hold or have completed another postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible.

Is there a nationality restriction?

The published eligibility requirements do not specify a nationality, race or continental restriction.

The important geographic consideration is that applicants’ research should demonstrate knowledge or expertise concerning countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

What is the research proposal word limit?

The research proposal must be 2,000 words maximum.

Footnotes, endnotes and bibliographies may be included and do not count toward the 2,000-word maximum.

How long can the writing sample be?

The scholarly writing sample must be no longer than 50 pages and must be written in English.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Applicants must submit three letters of recommendation.

When is the application deadline?

The main deadline is September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Recommendation letters have a later deadline of September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

When are the results expected?

Harvard anticipates announcing awards in December 2026.

Important Tips for Prospective Applicants

Applicants interested in this opportunity should begin preparing well before the deadline.

Start With the Research Proposal

Because the proposal has a strict 2,000-word limit, applicants should allow sufficient time to develop and revise it.

Contact Recommenders Early

Three confidential recommendation letters are required, and recommenders need time to upload their letters after the application is submitted.

Applicants should therefore approach potential recommenders early rather than waiting until the application deadline approaches.

Request Official Academic Records Early

Applicants from universities outside the United States should contact their registrars early to determine what official transcript-like documentation is available.

This is particularly important for applicants who have completed graduate study at multiple institutions.

Choose a Strong Writing Sample

The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to conduct rigorous scholarly research and communicate complex ideas effectively.

Applicants should select a piece that best represents their research abilities and aligns, where appropriate, with their broader scholarly profile.

Check Every Requirement Before Submission

Because Harvard does not accept late applications and incomplete applications can be disadvantaged during selection, applicants should ensure that every required component is prepared and submitted correctly.

Official Application Information

The official Harvard Academy information confirms the September 18, 2026 deadline, the eligibility requirements, the two-year appointment, the $80,000 annual stipend, the $6,000 annual research support and the application requirements.

Applicants should always consult the official Harvard Academy information before submitting their application because requirements and procedures can change.

Conclusion

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2026–2027 is a highly competitive opportunity for recent PhD recipients and advanced doctoral candidates in the social sciences who are developing innovative research focused on countries or regions outside the United States or Canada. Through a two-year in-residence appointment at Harvard University, selected scholars receive substantial financial support, research assistance, mentorship and access to an interdisciplinary academic community. With an annual stipend of $80,000, $6,000 in annual research support, and opportunities to participate in seminars, workshops, presentations and other scholarly activities, the program provides an environment designed to help promising researchers establish the foundations for long-term academic and international careers.  However, applicants should take note of the strict eligibility requirements and deadlines. The main application must be submitted by September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT, while recommendation letters must arrive by September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT. Harvard does not accept late applications.

For researchers who meet the requirements and have a strong, original research agenda grounded in social science and regional or country expertise, the Harvard Academy Scholars Program can provide an important platform for advancing their scholarship and becoming part of a distinguished international research community.

item.content:encoded:
The La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship 2026–2027 is a highly competitive international scholarship opportunity for outstanding students who want to study at La Trobe University in Australia. The scholarship provides either a 50% or 100% reduction in total course tuition fees, giving successful international students the opportunity to significantly reduce the cost of their undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree.

Recognising that future leaders demonstrate excellence beyond the classroom, La Trobe University considers not only academic achievement but also extracurricular involvement, sports, community engagement, leadership and the applicant’s potential to create meaningful change in their field or community.

The scholarship is available to eligible international students commencing an eligible course at La Trobe University’s Victorian campuses in 2026 or 2027.

La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship 2026–2027 Overview

The Vice-Chancellor Scholarship is La Trobe University’s most prestigious scholarship for international students. It is designed to recognise high-achieving students who have demonstrated exceptional academic performance and a commitment to making a positive difference beyond their studies.

Successful recipients receive a substantial tuition fee reduction and also become part of La Trobe University’s international student community and student ambassador program.

What Does the La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship Cover?

The scholarship provides either a 50% or 100% reduction in the total course tuition fee.

This means that successful students may receive either half or the full amount of their eligible course tuition fees covered through the scholarship.

The scholarship is applied as an upfront discount to annual tuition fees beginning from the first semester and continues for the duration of the course, provided that the recipient continues to satisfy the applicable scholarship conditions.

The scholarship does not represent a cash payment to the student. Instead, it reduces the tuition fees payable to La Trobe University.

Recipients must also accept their university offer and pay the required reduced deposit within the specified timeframe to confirm the scholarship. Failure to satisfy the conditions or make the required payment on time may result in the scholarship being withdrawn.

Who Is the La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship For?

The scholarship is designed for high-achieving international students who demonstrate excellence both academically and beyond academics.

La Trobe University is particularly interested in applicants who have demonstrated achievements or meaningful involvement in areas such as:

  • Academic excellence
  • Leadership
  • Community engagement
  • Extracurricular activities
  • Sports
  • Social impact
  • Personal initiative
  • Contribution to their community
  • Potential to create positive change after graduation

Therefore, applicants should not view this scholarship as an academic-performance-only award. The university specifically considers the broader impact and potential of candidates.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship, applicants must satisfy the university’s eligibility requirements.

1. Be an international student

Applicants must be citizens of a country other than Australia or New Zealand.

Applicants must also not hold a humanitarian visa or another permanent visa in Australia.

This makes the scholarship particularly relevant to students from countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Latin America and other regions who intend to pursue higher education in Australia.

2. Be a full-fee-paying student

Applicants must be full fee-paying students and must not be sponsored.

The scholarship is therefore intended for eligible international students who are responsible for paying international tuition fees before the scholarship reduction is applied.

3. Apply for an eligible course

Applicants must apply for direct entry into one of La Trobe University’s eligible courses.

Not every course is necessarily covered by the scholarship. Prospective applicants should therefore check La Trobe University’s current list of courses offering international scholarships before submitting their application.

4. Commence studies in 2026 or 2027

Applicants must be commencing their studies at one of La Trobe University’s Victorian campuses during an eligible 2026 or 2027 intake.

The scholarship cannot be deferred to 2028.

5. Meet English language requirements

Applicants must satisfy La Trobe University’s English language requirements as well as any other conditions specified in their offer letter.

6. Obtain an offer from La Trobe University

Applicants must have received an offer letter from La Trobe University before being considered for the scholarship.

The university notes that exceptions may be possible where approved by La Trobe.

Applicants must also successfully complete the university’s Genuine Student assessment, including required financial checks, before they can be considered for the scholarship.

7. Meet the academic requirement

Candidates must demonstrate outstanding academic performance.

The scholarship specifies a minimum Weighted Average Mark (WAM) of 80.

WAM is an average that takes into account the credit-point value of completed subjects. It is calculated based on the actual marks achieved in the subjects completed in a student’s course.

Academic performance is an important component of the selection process, and applicants should therefore ensure that their academic history is clearly presented.

How Are Scholarship Recipients Selected?

The La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship is highly competitive.

Eligible applicants are assessed based on several factors, including:

Outstanding academic performance

Academic achievement is one of the central selection criteria. Applicants need to demonstrate a strong academic record and meet the required minimum WAM.

English language proficiency

Applicants must satisfy La Trobe University’s English language requirements.

Written statement

Applicants must submit a written statement of no more than 250 words answering the following question:

“Beyond academic achievement, what specific difference do you hope to make in your field or community after completing your degree at La Trobe University?”

This statement provides applicants with an opportunity to demonstrate their ambitions, leadership potential and commitment to creating meaningful change.

A strong statement should connect the applicant’s academic goals with their future contribution to their profession, community or wider society.

Final selection

After the application deadline, eligible applicants are ranked and shortlisted according to their WAM.

Shortlisted candidates may then be invited to participate in a final selection round. Depending on the selection process, applicants may be asked to provide additional information, participate in an interview or submit a video.

The final number of scholarship recipients is determined by La Trobe University following its evaluation process.

Scholarship Benefits

The La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship provides several important benefits to successful international students.

1. Up to 100% tuition fee reduction

The most significant benefit is the potential for a 100% reduction in total course tuition fees.

Selected applicants may alternatively receive a 50% tuition fee reduction.

2. Reduced financial burden

International university tuition can represent a substantial financial commitment. A 50% or 100% tuition fee reduction can significantly reduce the overall cost of obtaining a degree in Australia.

3. Study at La Trobe University

Recipients become part of an internationally connected Australian university environment and gain access to La Trobe’s academic and student community.

4. Student ambassador opportunities

Scholarship recipients will become part of the La Trobe University student ambassador program.

Through this program, students can develop professional skills, expand their networks and gain experiences that can support their future careers.

5. Leadership and networking opportunities

The scholarship is intended to support students who have demonstrated the potential to become future leaders.

Recipients can benefit from being part of a community of high-achieving international students while developing their professional and leadership networks.

La Trobe University Campuses

The scholarship is available across eligible La Trobe University Victorian campuses, including:

  • Albury-Wodonga Campus
  • Bendigo Campus
  • Melbourne Campus
  • City Campus
  • Mildura Campus
  • Shepparton Campus

Applicants should confirm that their intended course is available at an eligible campus and qualifies for the scholarship before applying.

Application Deadlines for 2026 and 2027 Intakes

The scholarship has different application deadlines depending on the study intake and whether the applicant is located inside or outside Australia.

Because deadlines vary according to the applicant’s location and intended intake, applicants should carefully identify the appropriate deadline before submitting their application.

Summer / Term 6 2026

For applicants commencing in Summer / Term 6 2026:

  • Middle East and East Asia: 31 August 2026
  • All other international students located outside Australia: 14 September 2026
  • International students located in Australia: 21 October 2026

Scholarship award announcements are scheduled as follows:

  • Middle East and East Asia: 14 September 2026
  • Other international students outside Australia: 21 September 2026
  • International students in Australia: 23 October 2026

Semester 1, 2027

For applicants commencing in Semester 1, 2027:

  • International students outside Australia: 14 December 2026
  • International students located in Australia: 17 February 2027

Scholarship award announcements are scheduled for:

  • International students outside Australia: 22 December 2026
  • International students in Australia: 19 February 2027

Semester 2, 2027

For applicants commencing in Semester 2, 2027:

  • International students outside Australia: 17 May 2027
  • International students located in Australia: 1 July 2027

Scholarship award announcements are scheduled for:

  • International students outside Australia: 25 May 2027
  • International students in Australia: 2 July 2027

Overall closing date: 1 July 2027

Applicants should note that scholarship dates are subject to change. La Trobe University states that any changes will be communicated accordingly.

The 250-Word Scholarship Statement

One of the most important parts of the application is the written statement.

Applicants are asked:

“Beyond academic achievement, what specific difference do you hope to make in your field or community after completing your degree at La Trobe University?”

The statement is limited to 250 words, meaning applicants need to communicate their goals clearly and strategically.

A strong response should demonstrate:

  • The applicant’s professional ambitions
  • The problem they want to address
  • How their proposed degree will equip them to create change
  • The community or field they intend to serve
  • Their long-term contribution
  • Their motivation for studying at La Trobe University
  • The connection between their academic plans and future impact

Applicants should avoid simply repeating information already included in their academic application. Instead, the statement should help the selection committee understand the candidate’s purpose, vision and potential contribution.

Important Scholarship Conditions

Successful recipients must comply with the scholarship’s conditions throughout their studies.

Full-time enrolment

Recipients must maintain full-time enrolment at La Trobe University.

Satisfactory academic progress

Students must continue to demonstrate satisfactory academic progress throughout their studies.

Failure to meet academic or other scholarship requirements may affect continuation of the scholarship.

Participation in international scholarship activities

Recipients are required to participate in International Scholarship Program events during their studies in Australia.

No other La Trobe scholarship

No deferral to 2028

Acceptance deposit

Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a complete profile that demonstrates:

  • Leadership potential

  • A compelling reason for pursuing the chosen degree

  • Strong English language proficiency
  • A well-written scholarship statement

Applicants who can demonstrate how their education will translate into meaningful contributions to their profession or community may be better positioned to distinguish themselves during the selection process.

Key Takeaways

The La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship represents a major funding opportunity for high-achieving international students seeking to study in Australia.

The scholarship offers:

  • A 50% or 100% tuition fee reduction
  • Study opportunities at eligible La Trobe University Victorian campuses
  • Eligibility for selected undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs
  • Access to the La Trobe student ambassador program
  • Opportunities to develop leadership skills and professional networks
  • Recognition of academic achievement as well as extracurricular and community contributions

However, applicants should remember that eligibility does not guarantee selection. The scholarship is competitive, and candidates must demonstrate outstanding academic performance, meet the required WAM, satisfy university admission requirements and submit a compelling 250-word statement.

Most importantly, prospective applicants should begin preparing well before their relevant deadline because they must first secure admission and receive an offer before being considered for the scholarship.

Conclusion

The La Trobe Vice-Chancellor Scholarship 2026–2027 is a significant opportunity for outstanding international students who want to pursue an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree in Australia while substantially reducing their tuition costs.

With a scholarship value of 50% or 100% of total course tuition fees, the program can make a major difference to the financial cost of studying at La Trobe University. Beyond financial support, recipients join a globally connected university community and participate in the La Trobe student ambassador program, providing opportunities to develop leadership capabilities and professional networks.

The scholarship is particularly suited to students who can demonstrate more than strong grades. La Trobe University is looking for future leaders who have excelled academically while also making contributions through extracurricular activities, sports, community engagement and other forms of leadership.

Eligible international students should therefore begin preparing their university admission, academic documentation and 250-word impact statement early. Because application deadlines vary according to intake and location, applicants should identify the correct deadline for their circumstances and submit both their course and scholarship applications on time.

item.content:encoded:
Introduction to the FAO Green Cities Network

Cities are at the heart of some of the world’s most urgent environmental, social and economic challenges. Rapid urbanization, climate change, food insecurity, pollution, biodiversity loss and declining access to green spaces are increasingly affecting the quality of life of people living in urban areas. The FAO Green Cities Network is an international community of cities working to address these challenges by integrating nature, food systems, forestry and sustainable economic development into urban planning and development. Led by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the Green Cities Network brings together cities that are committed to transforming urban and peri-urban areas through practical solutions that can generate economic, social and environmental benefits simultaneously. The initiative recognizes that urban development does not have to come at the expense of nature. Instead, cities can use trees, forests, agriculture, green spaces and sustainable bioeconomy approaches to create healthier environments, improve food security, strengthen local economies and make communities more resilient to climate change.

Currently, more than 300 cities are benefiting from the initiative. The Network also includes cities affiliated through the joint FAO and Arbor Day Foundation Tree Cities of the World programme.

What Is the FAO Green Cities Network?

The FAO Green Cities Network is a global community of cities committed to making urban and peri-urban environments greener, healthier, more inclusive and sustainable.

The Network is designed around the idea that urban greening should not be treated as an isolated environmental activity. Instead, cities can integrate different sectors and strategies to address several challenges at the same time.

For example, planting and protecting trees in cities can:

  • Improve air quality.
  • Provide shade and reduce the effects of urban heat.
  • Support biodiversity.
  • Help manage rainwater.
  • Improve the appearance and livability of urban neighbourhoods.
  • Create recreational spaces.
  • Contribute to climate adaptation and mitigation.
  • Improve people’s physical and mental well-being.

Similarly, urban agriculture can help cities strengthen local food systems while providing employment opportunities, improving access to fresh food and making productive use of available urban and peri-urban land.

The Network therefore promotes approaches that connect environmental sustainability with food security, public health, economic development and social well-being.

The FAO Green Cities Initiative

The FAO Green Cities Network is at the centre of the broader Green Cities Initiative (GCI).

The Green Cities Initiative began in 2020 with an ambitious objective: to help generate tangible improvements in the health and well-being of people and the surrounding environment in 1,000 cities by 2030.

The initiative recognizes the growing importance of cities in addressing global challenges. As urban populations continue to grow, decisions made by city authorities can have a major impact on food systems, climate resilience, biodiversity, public health and the environment.

Through the Green Cities Initiative, FAO works with cities to promote practical and integrated solutions that can make urban areas more sustainable while improving the lives of residents.

The Green Cities Network provides an important platform for this work by connecting participating cities and enabling them to learn from one another.

Three Core Areas of the FAO Green Cities Network

The FAO Green Cities Network promotes integrated solutions and strategies across three major areas.

1. Urban and Peri-Urban Forestry

Urban and peri-urban forestry is one of the central pillars of the Green Cities Network.

It focuses on the planning, management, protection and development of trees and forests in and around cities.

Urban trees can provide a wide range of environmental and social benefits. They can help cities respond to rising temperatures, improve air quality, create shade, support wildlife and increase access to green spaces.

Urban and peri-urban forests can include:

  • Street trees.
  • Public parks.
  • Community forests.
  • Urban woodlands.
  • Trees around public buildings.
  • Green corridors.
  • Trees and vegetation in residential areas.
  • Forested areas surrounding cities.

Effective urban forestry requires more than simply planting trees. Cities need to consider where trees should be planted, which species are appropriate, how trees will be maintained, how green spaces can be protected and how residents can participate in urban greening efforts.

Through integrated urban forestry strategies, cities can make their environments more resilient and improve the quality of life of their populations.

2. Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture

The second major area promoted by the Network is urban and peri-urban agriculture.

Urban agriculture refers broadly to food production and related agricultural activities taking place within cities, while peri-urban agriculture takes place in areas surrounding urban centres.

As cities expand, agricultural spaces near urban areas can become increasingly important for food systems.

Urban and peri-urban agriculture can contribute to:

  • Local food production.
  • Improved access to fresh food.
  • Food security.
  • Livelihood creation.
  • Community participation.
  • Sustainable use of urban land.
  • Environmental improvement.
  • Greater resilience of local food systems.

Urban agriculture can take many forms, including community gardens, rooftop gardens, small-scale farms and other food-growing initiatives adapted to urban environments.

When incorporated into urban planning, these approaches can help cities develop food systems that are more connected to local communities.

3. Sustainable Bioeconomy

The third core area is the sustainable bioeconomy.

A sustainable bioeconomy seeks to make responsible use of biological resources while supporting economic development and environmental sustainability.

Within the context of green cities, bioeconomy approaches can help cities explore how biological resources, organic materials and related processes can contribute to more sustainable economic and environmental systems.

This can involve encouraging approaches that reduce waste, use resources more efficiently and support environmentally responsible economic activities.

The objective is not simply economic growth, but growth that takes environmental limits and long-term sustainability into account.

Why the FAO Green Cities Network Matters

The FAO Green Cities Network is important because cities are increasingly becoming key locations for addressing global sustainability challenges.

Urban areas consume substantial amounts of resources and are closely connected to food, energy, transportation, housing, economic activity and environmental systems.

At the same time, cities can provide opportunities to implement solutions at scale.

A successful urban greening project can potentially benefit thousands or even millions of residents. Similarly, improvements to local food systems, urban forests and green infrastructure can have effects that extend beyond individual neighbourhoods.

The Green Cities Network therefore encourages cities to think about sustainability in an integrated way.

Rather than addressing food security, climate change, public health and biodiversity separately, cities can pursue strategies that contribute to several objectives simultaneously.

Benefits of Participating in the Green Cities Network

Cities involved in the Green Cities Network can benefit from being part of an international community focused on sustainable urban development. Some of the key benefits associated with the Network include:

Knowledge Exchange

Cities can share experiences, approaches and lessons learned from implementing urban greening initiatives. This can help local authorities understand what has worked in other locations and consider how successful approaches could be adapted to their own circumstances.

City-to-City Collaboration

The Network encourages collaboration between cities. City officials and other stakeholders can learn from peers working on similar challenges, potentially creating opportunities for cooperation and the exchange of practical knowledge.

Recognition of Successful Initiatives

The Network recognizes cities that demonstrate leadership in implementing innovative and successful greening initiatives. This recognition can help highlight effective urban sustainability practices and demonstrate what cities can achieve when environmental considerations are integrated into development planning.

Improved Urban Environments

The broader objective of the initiative is to contribute to healthier and more sustainable urban environments. Urban forests, agricultural initiatives and sustainable bioeconomy approaches can all contribute to improving the relationship between cities, people and nature.

Contribution to Community Well-Being

Green cities can provide residents with better access to nature, healthier environments and opportunities for recreation and community participation. Urban greening can therefore contribute not only to environmental objectives but also to people’s health and quality of life.

Connection Between the Green Cities Network and the Sustainable Development Goals

The FAO Green Cities Network contributes directly to the achievement of several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Among the goals particularly connected to the initiative are:

SDG 2: Zero Hunger

Urban and peri-urban agriculture can contribute to food security by supporting local food production and strengthening urban food systems.

SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being

Access to trees, parks and other green spaces can contribute to healthier urban environments and improve opportunities for recreation and well-being.

Reducing environmental pressures and improving the quality of urban surroundings can also contribute to healthier communities.

SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities

The Green Cities Network has a particularly strong connection to SDG 11 because its central focus is on creating more sustainable and resilient urban communities.

Urban forestry, sustainable agriculture and green infrastructure can all contribute to better-planned and more livable cities.

SDG 13: Climate Action

Trees, forests and other forms of urban vegetation can contribute to climate mitigation and adaptation. Green infrastructure can also help cities respond to challenges such as extreme heat and other climate-related pressures.

SDG 15: Life on Land

Urban and peri-urban forests and green spaces can provide habitats for plants and animals and contribute to biodiversity conservation.  Protecting and expanding urban nature can therefore help cities contribute to broader efforts to protect terrestrial ecosystems.

The Tree Cities of the World Connection

The FAO Green Cities Network includes cities affiliated through the joint FAO and Arbor Day Foundation Tree Cities of the World programme. Tree Cities of the World provides recognition to cities that demonstrate a commitment to maintaining and improving their urban forests. The connection between the two initiatives highlights the importance of trees and urban forestry within the wider movement toward greener cities. Cities interested in understanding which locations are part of the Tree Cities of the World programme can consult its city directory to explore participating cities.

Who Can Benefit From the FAO Green Cities Network?

The Green Cities Network is particularly relevant to cities and local authorities interested in developing sustainable urban policies and practical greening initiatives.

It can be relevant to stakeholders working in areas such as:

  • Urban planning.
  • Environmental management.
  • Forestry.
  • Agriculture.
  • Food systems.
  • Climate action.
  • Biodiversity conservation.
  • Public health.
  • Sustainable development.
  • Local economic development.
  • Green infrastructure.
  • Community development.

The initiative can also provide useful knowledge and examples for organizations, institutions, researchers and other stakeholders working with cities on sustainable development.

Why Integrated Urban Solutions Are Important

One of the most important aspects of the FAO Green Cities Network is its emphasis on integrated solutions.

Urban challenges are interconnected.

For example, climate change can increase temperatures in cities. Higher temperatures can affect human health and make urban areas less comfortable. Trees and green spaces can provide shade and help address urban heat while simultaneously supporting biodiversity and improving the appearance of neighbourhoods.

Likewise, urban agriculture can contribute to food production while providing livelihood opportunities and making productive use of available land.

This demonstrates why integrated approaches can be more effective than treating every urban challenge as a completely separate issue.

The Green Cities approach encourages cities to look for solutions capable of delivering several benefits at the same time.

The Vision for Greener Cities by 2030

The Green Cities Initiative’s goal of contributing to tangible improvements in 1,000 cities by 2030 demonstrates the scale of FAO’s ambition.

The objective is not simply to increase the number of trees or green spaces in cities. The broader vision is to improve the relationship between urban development, human well-being and the natural environment.

Achieving this vision requires cooperation among governments, local authorities, communities, technical experts and other stakeholders.

It also requires cities to consider sustainability when making decisions about land use, food systems, environmental management and urban development.

How the Green Cities Network Can Support Urban Transformation

The Network provides a framework through which cities can become part of a wider international movement for sustainable urban development.

Its approach can help cities:

  1. Identify urban environmental challenges and consider how they affect residents and ecosystems.
  2. Develop integrated strategies that connect environmental, social and economic objectives.
  3. Promote urban and peri-urban forestry to expand and improve urban green spaces.
  4. Strengthen urban food systems through urban and peri-urban agriculture.
  5. Explore sustainable bioeconomy opportunities that support responsible resource use.
  6. Exchange knowledge with other cities facing similar challenges.
  7. Recognize and promote successful initiatives that demonstrate effective urban greening.
  8. Contribute to global sustainability goals, particularly those related to food security, health, sustainable cities, climate action and biodiversity.

Is There a Deadline to Join the FAO Green Cities Network?

No specific application deadline is provided in the information supplied for this article. The Green Cities Initiative is a long-term programme with a target of supporting improvements in 1,000 cities by 2030, rather than a conventional short-term opportunity with a single closing date. Anyone interested in participation should consult the official FAO Green Cities Initiative and Green Cities Network information for the latest requirements, procedures and opportunities for engagement.

To apply click HERE

Learn more HERE

Why Cities Should Pay Attention to the Green Cities Movement

The future of sustainable development will depend significantly on what happens in cities. As urban populations grow, cities will need to find ways to provide food, housing, economic opportunities and essential services while protecting natural resources and reducing environmental pressures. The FAO Green Cities Network demonstrates how urban areas can approach these challenges through nature-based and integrated solutions. Its focus on urban forestry, urban and peri-urban agriculture and sustainable bioeconomy creates opportunities to connect environmental protection with economic and social development. For cities looking to become more resilient, healthy and sustainable, participation in international knowledge-sharing networks can provide valuable access to ideas, experience and examples from other urban communities.

Conclusion

The FAO Green Cities Network represents an important global effort to transform cities into greener, healthier and more sustainable places to live and work. Through its three core areas — urban and peri-urban forestry, urban and peri-urban agriculture, and sustainable bioeconomy — the Network promotes solutions capable of delivering environmental, social and economic benefits simultaneously. With more than 300 cities already benefiting from the initiative and the broader Green Cities Initiative targeting tangible improvements in 1,000 cities by 2030, FAO is supporting a significant international movement toward more sustainable urban development. The Network also contributes to major global priorities, including the Sustainable Development Goals on zero hunger, health and well-being, sustainable cities, climate action and life on land. Ultimately, the FAO Green Cities Network demonstrates that cities can be part of the solution to global environmental and social challenges. By integrating trees, forests, agriculture, biodiversity and sustainable economic approaches into urban development, cities can create healthier communities while building greater resilience for the future.

item.content:encoded:
Young people interested in international affairs, diplomacy, gender equality, sustainable development, global policy, and the United Nations have an opportunity to become part of the Young Diplomats of Canada (YDC) 2027 United Nations delegations.

YDC is currently recruiting delegates for two major United Nations-related engagements in 2027: the 71st Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71) and the High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF 2027).

These delegations provide an opportunity for young people to engage with major global policy discussions and contribute to conversations surrounding some of the world’s most pressing development and social challenges.

The two United Nations events focus on important areas of global policy, including gender equality, women’s and girls’ empowerment, sustainable development, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), youth participation, international cooperation, and implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

The application deadline for the current recruitment round is Friday, September 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (PT).

About Young Diplomats of Canada

Young Diplomats of Canada (YDC) is a youth-focused organization that works to empower young people and elevate youth voices within the global policy arena.

According to the organization’s recruitment information, YDC is operated by an all-youth, all-volunteer executive team made up of individuals from across Canada.

The organization focuses on:

  • Creating opportunities for young people to engage with international affairs
  • Building networks among young leaders
  • Elevating youth perspectives in global policy discussions
  • Connecting young people with international institutions and policy processes
  • Opening doors for youth participation in international diplomacy and policy

Through its delegations, YDC gives participants an opportunity to engage with important international policy discussions and gain exposure to the work taking place around the United Nations.

2027 United Nations Delegations

For 2027, YDC is recruiting delegates for two significant United Nations platforms:

  1. The 71st Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71)
  2. The High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF 2027)

Both events are scheduled to take place at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, United States, although the HLPF’s exact dates have not yet been confirmed by the United Nations.

1. 71st Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71)

The Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) is the United Nations’ principal global forum dedicated to advancing gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.

The 71st session, known as CSW71, is scheduled to take place from 8–19 March 2027.

Location: United Nations Headquarters, New York, United States

CSW71 Priority Theme

The stated priority theme for CSW71 is:

“Accelerating the achievement of gender equality and the empowerment of all women and girls in the context of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.”

This theme connects gender equality with the broader United Nations Sustainable Development Agenda.

For prospective delegates, this means that an interest in issues such as women’s rights, gender equality, social development, public policy, international development, human rights, and the Sustainable Development Goals may be particularly relevant to the discussions surrounding the delegation.

Why CSW71 Matters

Gender equality remains a major component of the global development agenda.

Women’s and girls’ access to education, economic opportunities, political participation, healthcare, safety, leadership, and decision-making can have significant implications for sustainable development.

CSW provides an international platform where governments, civil society organizations, advocates, experts, and other stakeholders can participate in discussions concerning these issues.

Being connected to a YDC delegation focused on CSW71 can therefore expose participants to international discussions around gender equality and the implementation of global development commitments.

2. High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF 2027)

YDC is also recruiting delegates for the High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF 2027).

The HLPF is described as the United Nations’ central platform for reviewing progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

It brings together a wide range of stakeholders, including:

  • Governments
  • Civil society
  • Youth
  • Academia
  • The private sector
  • International development actors
  • Other stakeholders involved in sustainable development

The purpose of the forum is to review progress toward the SDGs and support the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

HLPF 2027 Details

Location: United Nations Headquarters, New York, United States

Date: July 2027

Official dates: To be confirmed by the United Nations

Because the official dates have not yet been announced, applicants should monitor updates from YDC and the United Nations for further information.

What Participants Can Gain from the Opportunity

Participation in an international United Nations delegation can provide valuable exposure to global policy processes and international development discussions.

Potential benefits of participating include:

1. Exposure to United Nations Policy Discussions

Delegates can gain first-hand exposure to discussions taking place around major international policy priorities.

This can be particularly valuable for young people interested in:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Public policy
  • International development
  • Human rights
  • Gender equality
  • Sustainable development
  • Global affairs
  • Multilateral cooperation

2. International Networking Opportunities

United Nations-related events bring together people and organizations from different backgrounds and areas of expertise.

Participation can therefore provide opportunities to develop professional and international networks.

3. Understanding Global Development Processes

The CSW and HLPF address major international policy issues.

A delegate can gain a better understanding of how international organizations, governments, civil society, youth representatives, academics, and other stakeholders contribute to global policy discussions.

4. Youth Representation

YDC places a strong emphasis on empowering young people and elevating youth voices in the global policy arena.

The delegation model therefore provides a platform through which young people can engage with international discussions.

5. Professional and Leadership Development

Participation in an international delegation can help participants develop skills and experiences relevant to careers involving:

  • Diplomacy
  • Government
  • International organizations
  • Non-governmental organizations
  • Public policy
  • Advocacy
  • International development
  • Sustainability
  • Gender equality
  • Youth leadership

6. Engagement with the Sustainable Development Goals

The HLPF is directly connected to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Applicants who are passionate about sustainable development can gain valuable exposure to how progress toward the SDGs is reviewed and discussed at the international level.

Who Should Consider Applying?

Although the announcement does not provide a complete eligibility checklist, the opportunity may be particularly relevant to young people interested in international policy and global affairs.

Potentially relevant backgrounds and interests include:

  • International relations
  • Political science
  • Development studies
  • Public policy
  • Law
  • Gender studies
  • Human rights
  • International development
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Social development
  • Youth advocacy
  • Diplomacy
  • Global governance
  • Sustainable Development Goals
  • Civil society
  • Non-governmental organizations

Applicants should, however, review the YDC application form and FAQ to determine whether they meet the organization’s specific eligibility requirements.

The announcement provided does not explicitly state a complete age requirement, citizenship requirement, nationality requirement, or country eligibility list. Therefore, applicants should verify these details before applying.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 United Nations delegation recruitment is:

Friday, September 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (PT).

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline.

Because the deadline is given in Pacific Time, applicants living in other countries should convert the deadline to their local time and avoid waiting until the final hours to submit an application.

APPLY HERE

How to Apply

Interested applicants can apply through the official YDC application form.

The application form is identified by YDC as a bilingual application form.

Applicants should carefully complete all required sections and ensure that the information submitted accurately represents their background, interests, experiences, and motivation for participating.

It is advisable to review the application carefully before submission and make sure that all required questions have been answered.

For more information about this opportunity visit Young Diplomats of Canada (YDC) Website HERE

Also visit the OFY Website HERE for more global opportunities

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity: 2027 United Nations Delegations

Organization: Young Diplomats of Canada

Focus: International affairs, gender equality and sustainable development

Delegation 1: 71st Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71)

CSW71 Dates: 8–19 March 2027

CSW71 Location: United Nations Headquarters, New York

CSW71 Theme: Accelerating gender equality and empowerment of women and girls within the 2030 Agenda

Delegation 2: High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF 2027)

HLPF Date: July 2027

HLPF Location: United Nations Headquarters, New York

HLPF Official Dates: To be confirmed

Application: Online

Application Form: Bilingual

Deadline: September 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PT

Organization Structure: All-youth, all-volunteer executive

Important Information for Applicants

Applicants should understand that this is not simply an ordinary conference registration.

The opportunity is connected to YDC’s United Nations delegation program, meaning prospective applicants should familiarize themselves with the organization, its mission, its delegation model, and the responsibilities associated with participating as a delegate.

Before applying, candidates should also carefully review the organization’s official information and FAQ to understand the application process and any requirements that may not be included in the recruitment announcement.

In particular, applicants should verify:

  • Specific eligibility requirements
  • Age requirements
  • Citizenship or residency requirements
  • Any requirements concerning Canadian affiliation
  • Delegate responsibilities
  • Selection criteria
  • Financial or participation costs
  • Travel requirements
  • Accommodation arrangements
  • Visa requirements where applicable
  • What expenses are covered or not covered
  • Any preparation expected before the United Nations meetings

These details are important because the recruitment announcement does not specify them.

Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable for Aspiring Global Leaders

Young professionals and students increasingly seek opportunities that provide exposure beyond the classroom or workplace.

International policy platforms can provide an opportunity to understand how global institutions function and how international priorities are debated.

For someone interested in diplomacy, international development, public policy, gender equality, sustainability, or global governance, participation in a United Nations delegation could complement academic and professional experience.

The CSW71 delegation offers particular relevance for individuals interested in gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls, while the HLPF delegation is particularly relevant to people interested in sustainable development and the SDGs.

Together, the two delegations cover important dimensions of the international development agenda.

Preparation Tips for Applicants

Before submitting an application, prospective delegates should consider taking the following steps:

1. Research YDC

Understand the organization’s mission, delegation work, and approach to youth engagement.

2. Learn About the United Nations

Applicants should have a basic understanding of the United Nations system and the purpose of the relevant forum.

3. Research CSW71 or HLPF

Candidates should understand the specific purpose and priorities of the delegation they are interested in.

4. Connect Your Experience to the Opportunity

When completing an application, clearly demonstrate how your academic, professional, volunteer, leadership, advocacy, or community experiences relate to the opportunity.

5. Explain Your Motivation

Applicants should be able to clearly communicate why they want to participate and what they hope to contribute or learn.

6. Review the Application Before Submitting

Check that all required sections have been completed and that your responses are clear, relevant, and accurate.

7. Apply Early

Do not wait until the final day. Technical problems, incomplete responses, or time-zone confusion could create unnecessary problems close to the deadline.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the 2027 YDC United Nations Delegation opportunity?

It is a recruitment opportunity by Young Diplomats of Canada for delegates to participate in United Nations-related engagements in 2027, specifically CSW71 and HLPF 2027.

When is CSW71 taking place?

The 71st Commission on the Status of Women is scheduled for 8–19 March 2027 at United Nations Headquarters in New York.

When will HLPF 2027 take place?

HLPF 2027 is scheduled for July 2027 at United Nations Headquarters in New York. The official dates have not yet been confirmed by the United Nations.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is Friday, September 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (PT).

Where will the events take place?

Both events are identified as taking place at United Nations Headquarters in New York, United States.

Is the application available online?

Yes. YDC provides an online application form, identified as bilingual.

Is YDC currently recruiting executive team members?

No. According to the announcement, YDC is not currently recruiting new Executive Team members.

Does the announcement state who is eligible by country?

The provided announcement does not give a complete country-by-country eligibility list. Applicants should consult the official application form and YDC’s FAQ for the authoritative eligibility requirements.

Does the announcement specify an age requirement?

No specific age requirement is included in the information provided. Applicants should verify this directly through YDC’s official application materials.

Does the opportunity cover travel and accommodation?

The information provided does not specify what expenses are covered. Applicants should check YDC’s official materials or contact the organization for details concerning participation costs, travel, accommodation, and other expenses.

Conclusion

The Young Diplomats of Canada 2027 United Nations Delegations offer an opportunity for young people interested in international affairs and global policy to seek participation in two major United Nations platforms: the 71st Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71) and the High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF 2027).

CSW71 will focus on accelerating progress toward gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls within the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while HLPF 2027 will provide a platform for reviewing progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals and advancing implementation of the 2030 Agenda.

For candidates interested in diplomacy, international development, gender equality, sustainable development, youth leadership, public policy, human rights, or global affairs, this could be a valuable opportunity to pursue.

Interested applicants should carefully review the official requirements, prepare their application thoroughly, and submit it before the September 4, 2026 deadline at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.

The opportunity provides an avenue for young people to engage with international policy discussions, expand their networks, strengthen their understanding of global development, and potentially contribute to conversations taking place around some of the world’s most important development priorities.
