item.content:encoded:
The University of Pretoria (UP) has opened applications for the 2027 University of Pretoria Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary, an exciting doctoral funding opportunity for outstanding students from Commonwealth countries who wish to pursue full-time doctoral studies in South Africa.

The bursary has been established as part of South Africa’s participation in the Commonwealth Scholarship Plan and is intended to attract exceptional doctoral candidates whose research can contribute meaningfully to the University of Pretoria’s research mission.

For 2027, the University of Pretoria has made funding available for up to two doctoral scholarships specifically for eligible citizens of Commonwealth countries. The award is competitive, meaning applicants will be assessed against other eligible candidates, and meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee selection.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to high-achieving international students who are looking for doctoral-level funding at a leading research-intensive university in South Africa.

About the University of Pretoria Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary

The University of Pretoria is a research-intensive institution committed to developing high-level researchers and attracting talented doctoral candidates from around the world.

Through the 2027 Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary, the University is providing financial support to selected doctoral candidates from Commonwealth countries, excluding South African citizens and permanent residents.

The bursary supports the University’s broader commitment to research excellence while contributing to international academic collaboration under the Commonwealth Scholarship Plan.

A maximum of two doctoral scholarships will be awarded for the 2027 academic year.

Because the bursary is competitive, prospective applicants should ensure that they carefully review the official applicant guidelines, terms and conditions, and other supporting information before submitting an application.

Key Details of the 2027 UP Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary

Opportunity Details
Host institution University of Pretoria
Country South Africa
Study level Doctoral
Opportunity type Bursary/Scholarship
Funding category UP Internal Bursary
Target applicants Citizens of Commonwealth countries
South African citizens eligible? No
South African permanent residents eligible? No
Number of awards Up to two
Study mode Full-time
Duration Three years
Selection Competitive
Application period 3 August 2026 to 1 October 2026
Deadline 1 October 2026 at 23:59
Contact office Postgraduate Scholarship Office (PGSO)
Contact email pgbursary@up.ac.za
Campus Graduate Centre, Hatfield Campus

What Does the Bursary Offer?

The University of Pretoria has made funding available for up to two doctoral scholarships under this initiative.

The bursary is designed to support successful candidates undertaking a full-time three-year doctoral programme at the University of Pretoria.

However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the distinction between receiving the bursary and meeting the other financial and administrative requirements associated with studying in South Africa.

For example, successful awardees are specifically required to be able to pay for the medical insurance required for a South African study permit.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that every cost associated with international study and relocation will automatically be covered by the bursary.

Who Can Apply for the 2027 Commonwealth Doctoral Bursary?

The opportunity is specifically targeted at citizens of Commonwealth countries.

Applicants must be citizens of an eligible Commonwealth country and must not be South African citizens or permanent residents.

This makes the bursary particularly attractive to doctoral candidates from Commonwealth nations across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, the Pacific and other regions.

Applicants should carefully confirm that their country is a Commonwealth member before proceeding with an application.

South African Applicants Are Excluded

The University of Pretoria has expressly stated that:

  • South African citizens cannot apply.
  • South African permanent residents cannot apply.
  • The opportunity is intended for citizens of other Commonwealth countries.

Consequently, applicants should not submit an application if they fall within either of the excluded South African categories.

What Level of Study Is Supported?

The 2027 Commonwealth Bursary is specifically for doctoral-level study.

This means that it is intended for applicants seeking to undertake a PhD or other qualifying doctoral studies at the University of Pretoria.

It is therefore not an undergraduate scholarship, master’s scholarship, short-course funding opportunity or general student bursary.

Applicants should ensure that they meet the University of Pretoria’s academic admission requirements for their intended doctoral programme in addition to meeting the Commonwealth bursary requirements.

Full-Time Study Requirement

One of the important conditions of the opportunity is that successful awardees must undertake their doctoral studies on a full-time basis.

The bursary is structured around a three-year full-time period.

This requirement is especially important for applicants who are currently employed.

If an applicant is employed and needs permission or leave from their employer to undertake full-time doctoral studies, they must have the required permission or leave from their workplace at the time of applying, if applicable.

Applicants should therefore consider their employment circumstances carefully before applying.

Requirements for Applicants Who Are Currently Employed

Applicants who are currently working should pay particular attention to the requirement concerning their employment.

Successful awardees must be able to obtain the necessary permission or leave from their employer to take up the full-time three-year bursary.

This means that applicants who cannot obtain the required workplace permission may encounter difficulties in taking up the award.

If you are employed, it is therefore advisable to understand your employer’s policies regarding study leave, unpaid leave, sabbatical arrangements or other forms of permission for full-time doctoral study.

Study Permit Requirement

International applicants who are selected for the bursary must also ensure that they are eligible to apply for a South African study permit.

This is an important consideration because the bursary is intended for students from Commonwealth countries outside South Africa.

Applicants should therefore make sure that there are no circumstances that would prevent them from obtaining the appropriate immigration permission to study in South Africa.

Being eligible for the bursary does not necessarily mean that an applicant is automatically granted a study permit.

The study permit process is a separate requirement that successful international applicants must be able to satisfy.

Medical Insurance Requirement

Another important condition is the requirement relating to medical insurance.

Successful awardees must be able to pay for the medical insurance required for a study permit for 2027.

Prospective applicants should therefore budget for this requirement when planning their doctoral studies.

This is particularly important for international students because medical insurance can form part of the documentation and financial requirements associated with obtaining permission to study in South Africa.

How Competitive Is the Opportunity?

The University of Pretoria describes the Commonwealth Doctoral Bursary as a competitive award.

Only up to two doctoral scholarships are available.

This means that applicants should not rely solely on meeting the minimum eligibility conditions. Strong applicants should present a compelling academic and research profile and ensure that their application is complete and carefully prepared.

Prospective applicants should also pay close attention to the University’s doctoral admission requirements and the information contained in the official applicant guideline, terms and conditions.

Why Consider the University of Pretoria?

The University of Pretoria is recognised as a leading research-intensive institution and places significant emphasis on research and postgraduate development.

For doctoral candidates, studying at a research-intensive university can provide an opportunity to develop advanced research expertise while working within an academic environment focused on research and knowledge creation.

The Commonwealth Bursary also provides an opportunity for eligible international scholars to pursue doctoral studies in South Africa while participating in the broader Commonwealth academic and research ecosystem.

For candidates from Commonwealth countries who are interested in building an international academic or research career, the opportunity can therefore be worth serious consideration.

Important Conditions Applicants Should Know

Before applying, prospective candidates should take note of the following conditions:

  1. Only citizens of eligible Commonwealth countries can apply.
  2. South African citizens are excluded from the opportunity.
  3. South African permanent residents are also excluded.
  4. The bursary is for doctoral-level study.
  5. Successful candidates must undertake full-time doctoral study.
  6. The bursary is structured for three years of full-time study.
  7. Applicants who are employed must have the necessary permission or leave from their workplace to take up the full-time bursary, where applicable.
  8. Successful applicants must be eligible to apply for a South African study permit.
  9. Successful awardees must be able to pay for the medical insurance required for a 2027 study permit.
  10. Only up to two doctoral scholarships will be awarded.
  11. Selection is competitive, so meeting the basic eligibility criteria does not guarantee an award.

Application Deadline for the 2027 UP Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary

The application period shown by the University of Pretoria runs from 3 August 2026 until 1 October 2026.

Deadline: 1 October 2026 at 23:59

APPLY HERE 

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications.

International doctoral applicants may need to prepare several pieces of information and documentation, and last-minute submissions can create unnecessary risks if there are technical problems, missing documents or other application issues.

Prospective applicants are therefore encouraged to begin preparing well ahead of the deadline and carefully review the official applicant guidelines and terms and conditions.

For more information,see the Applicant Guide, terms and conditions.

For more Commonwealth scholarships, visit OFY Website HERE

Where Can Applicants Find the Official Information?

The University of Pretoria has provided additional documents for prospective applicants, including:

  • The 2027 UP Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary Flyer
  • The UP Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary Applicant Guideline, Terms and Conditions 2027

Applicants should read these official documents carefully because they contain important information governing the bursary.

The University’s official funding page should also be used as the primary reference for application information and any updates.

Official opportunity page: University of Pretoria – 2027 UP Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary.

Contact Information

Applicants who need clarification about the bursary can contact the University of Pretoria’s Postgraduate Scholarship Office.

Office: Postgraduate Scholarship Office (PGSO)

Location: Graduate Centre, Hatfield Campus

Division: Graduate Support Hub (GSH)

Department: Department of Research and Innovation

Email: pgbursary@up.ac.za

Applicants should use the official contact details provided by the University when seeking clarification about eligibility, application procedures or bursary requirements.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because only up to two awards are available, applicants should approach the opportunity strategically.

1. Confirm your Commonwealth citizenship

Before investing significant time in the application, confirm that you are a citizen of an eligible Commonwealth country.

Remember that South African citizens and permanent residents are specifically excluded.

2. Confirm your doctoral eligibility

Make sure you satisfy the academic and admission requirements for the doctoral programme you intend to pursue at the University of Pretoria.

The bursary requirement and university admission requirements should both be considered.

3. Review the official guidelines

Read the applicant guideline, terms and conditions and official bursary information carefully.

Do not rely on summaries from third-party websites alone.

4. Consider your employment situation

If you are employed, determine whether you can obtain the necessary permission or leave to undertake the required full-time doctoral programme.

5. Plan for the study permit

International students should investigate the requirements for obtaining a South African study permit and make sure they will be able to meet them if selected.

6. Budget for medical insurance

Remember that successful awardees must be able to pay for the medical insurance required for a 2027 study permit.

7. Start early

With only two awards available, applicants should give themselves enough time to prepare a strong and complete submission rather than rushing shortly before the deadline.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the 2027 UP Commonwealth Doctoral Bursary open to international students?

Yes. The bursary is specifically intended for citizens of Commonwealth countries other than South African citizens and permanent residents.

Can South African citizens apply?

No. South African citizens are expressly excluded.

Can South African permanent residents apply?

No. South African permanent residents are also excluded.

What level of study does the bursary support?

The bursary is intended for doctoral-level study.

How long is the bursary?

The successful awardees must be able to take up a full-time three-year bursary.

How many scholarships are available?

The University of Pretoria has made funding available for up to two doctoral scholarships.

Is the bursary competitive?

Yes. The University states that the awards will be granted on a competitive basis.

Do employed applicants need permission from their employers?

Where applicable, successful awardees must have the required permission or leave from their workplace to take up the full-time three-year bursary.

Do successful applicants need a South African study permit?

Successful international awardees must ensure that they are eligible to apply for a study permit.

Does the University pay for medical insurance?

Applicants should not assume that medical insurance is automatically covered. The University specifically states that successful awardees must be able to pay for the medical insurance required for a 2027 study permit.

When is the application deadline?

The stated deadline is 1 October 2026 at 23:59.

Conclusion

The 2027 University of Pretoria Doctoral Commonwealth Bursary presents a valuable opportunity for exceptional doctoral candidates from Commonwealth countries who want to pursue full-time doctoral studies at a leading research-intensive university in South Africa.

With funding available for up to two candidates, the opportunity is highly competitive. Eligible applicants should therefore ensure that they understand all requirements before applying, including the citizenship restrictions, doctoral study requirements, full-time three-year commitment, workplace permission where applicable, study permit eligibility and medical insurance requirements.

Applicants should also carefully review the University’s official applicant guideline, terms and conditions and bursary flyer before submitting an application.

For eligible Commonwealth citizens with strong academic and research ambitions, this bursary could provide an important pathway toward advanced doctoral education and research development at the University of Pretoria.

Deadline: 1 October 2026 at 23:59.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to begin preparing early and to rely on the official University of Pretoria funding information for the most accurate and up-to-date application instructions.

item.content:encoded:
The One Humanity Fellowship 2026 is a three-month fellowship opportunity for emerging writers and multimedia producers who are passionate about human rights, civic life, social change, culture, and stories that are often overlooked by mainstream international media.

Organized by We Are One Humanity (WAOH), the fellowship is designed to support storytellers who have meaningful ideas, experiences, perspectives, and stories to share but need editorial guidance and a platform to bring those stories to a wider global audience.

Unlike opportunities that simply provide participants with a byline or short-term exposure, the One Humanity Fellowship emphasizes a genuine editorial relationship. Selected fellows will work closely with experienced editors and field experts to develop and publish original work throughout the three-month program.

The fellowship welcomes different forms of storytelling, including journalism, analytical writing, personal essays, photography, short-form video, audio, and social media storytelling.

Applications are currently open, and interested applicants must submit their applications by August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).

About the One Humanity Fellowship

The One Humanity Fellowship is a three-month program created for writers and multimedia producers working at the intersection of human rights, civic life, and underreported stories.

The program recognizes that important stories do not always receive attention from major international media organizations. Many communities, particularly those in underrepresented regions, have experiences and perspectives that deserve to be documented and shared.

Through the fellowship, WAOH aims to provide emerging storytellers with the editorial support, mentorship, publication opportunities, and community they need to develop their voices and produce meaningful work.

Fellows will publish at least five original pieces during the three-month fellowship period. These pieces will be developed and published on a biweekly schedule.

The program is therefore suitable for individuals who are not simply looking for an opportunity to publish one article but who want to build an ongoing relationship with editors and develop their storytelling skills.

What Does the One Humanity Fellowship Offer?

Selected fellows will receive several forms of professional and editorial support throughout the program.

1. Publication and Global Exposure

Fellows will have their work published on the We Are One Humanity website.

Their work will also be distributed to WAOH’s global newsletter readership, giving fellows an opportunity to reach readers beyond their immediate communities.

For emerging writers and multimedia producers, this can provide valuable exposure and help demonstrate their ability to produce original work for an international audience.

2. Editorial Mentorship

Fellows will receive editorial mentorship from experienced WAOH editors.

This means participants will not be expected to develop their work completely on their own. Instead, they will have access to editorial guidance as they develop, refine, and prepare their pieces for publication.

This can be particularly valuable for emerging storytellers who want to improve areas such as:

  • Story development
  • Research and analysis
  • Writing structure
  • Narrative development
  • Editorial judgment
  • Clarity and communication
  • Audience engagement
  • Developing a distinctive storytelling voice

3. Expert Mentorship

In addition to editorial support, fellows will receive expert mentorship in their chosen field.

Participants will be matched with experts based on their interests within WAOH’s thematic areas.

This provides an opportunity for fellows to gain perspectives from individuals with experience or expertise relevant to the issues they want to explore.

4. Guest Speaking Opportunity

Fellows may also be invited to participate in a WAOH webinar as a guest speaker.

This gives selected fellows the possibility of discussing a topic related to their field of interest and expertise with a broader audience.

The opportunity can help participants strengthen their public communication and thought-leadership experience.

5. International Cohort Community

Fellows will become part of a cohort of storytellers working across different regions, formats, and perspectives.

Throughout the fellowship, participants will interact with one another and build connections with people who may have different cultural backgrounds, professional experiences, and approaches to storytelling.

This cohort environment can provide opportunities for:

  • Networking
  • Collaboration
  • Knowledge exchange
  • Cross-cultural learning
  • Professional relationship building
  • Exposure to different perspectives

6. $500 Stipend

Selected fellows will receive a stipend of $500 for their time and work during the fellowship.

The stipend recognizes the commitment required to participate in the program and produce work throughout the three-month period.

Who Should Apply for the One Humanity Fellowship?

The fellowship is open to emerging writers and multimedia producers at any career stage.

Importantly, applicants do not need to have a journalism degree or formal journalism training.

WAOH is primarily interested in applicants who demonstrate a genuine interest in the issues covered by the fellowship and who have something meaningful to say or show through their chosen storytelling format.

Strong applicants should demonstrate:

  • Genuine engagement with human rights or civic issues
  • A distinct writing, storytelling, or visual voice
  • A unique perspective on the issues they care about
  • An interest in telling stories that are often overlooked
  • The ability to commit to the three-month fellowship
  • The willingness to meet regular publication deadlines
  • An interest in developing original work with editorial support

The fellowship is particularly interested in people whose communities and stories are rarely represented in international media.

No Journalism Degree Required

One of the notable features of the One Humanity Fellowship is that applicants do not need a journalism degree or formal journalism training.

This makes the opportunity accessible to individuals who may have developed their storytelling abilities through personal experience, community work, advocacy, creative projects, independent writing, social media, photography, video production, audio production, or other forms of communication.

What matters is the applicant’s ability to demonstrate a genuine engagement with important human rights or civic issues and a distinctive perspective.

What Types of Storytellers Can Apply?

The fellowship accepts storytellers working across a wide range of formats.

These include:

  • Journalistic writing
  • Analytical articles
  • Personal essays
  • Photo essays
  • Short-form video
  • Audio storytelling
  • Social media stories
  • Other multimedia storytelling formats

This makes the program potentially suitable for writers, journalists, photographers, filmmakers, content creators, researchers, activists, communicators, and other storytellers who can bring important issues to life through their chosen medium.

One Humanity Fellowship Thematic Areas

Fellows will work within one or more of WAOH’s five major thematic areas.

The themes provide a framework for the type of work the organization is interested in, but they are not rigid assignments.

Applicants are encouraged to bring their own perspectives, regions, communities, experiences, and ideas to these broad areas.

1. Responding to Threats Against Democracy

This theme focuses on the challenges facing democratic principles and institutions around the world.

Potential areas of exploration include:

  • Political developments and democratic decline
  • Media suppression
  • Freedom of expression
  • Youth-led movements against corruption
  • Democratic backsliding
  • The ways elected leaders can weaken democratic institutions
  • Disinformation and misinformation
  • Artificial intelligence-generated content
  • The global battle for truth and reliable information
  • Religion and nationalism
  • The use of faith as a political tool
  • Concentration of wealth among technology billionaires and political elites
  • Corporate impunity
  • Situations where companies violate laws while governments fail to act

Applicants are not restricted to these examples. They can develop their own perspective on threats to democratic societies.

2. Moving Beyond Polarization

This theme explores ways societies can overcome division and develop greater understanding across different identities and perspectives.

Potential topics include:

  • Online hate
  • Digital dehumanization
  • The consequences of online hostility in the real world
  • Cancel culture
  • Accountability
  • Restorative justice
  • Religious minorities in secular societies
  • Islamophobia
  • Political and social polarization
  • The relationship between advocacy and opposing viewpoints

The theme is particularly relevant to storytellers interested in examining how communities can move beyond conflict and division.

3. Fighting for Human Rights

This thematic area focuses on issues that directly affect human rights and the wellbeing of communities.

Possible subjects include:

  • Deportation
  • Family separation
  • Climate migration
  • Communities displaced by floods, drought, and rising sea levels
  • Undocumented workers
  • Essential workers and the economies they support
  • Ongoing conflicts that receive limited international attention
  • Conflicts in Sudan, Myanmar, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
  • Exploitative supply chains
  • Fast fashion and its hidden human cost
  • Voting rights
  • Electoral integrity
  • What makes an election free and fair
  • Systemic oppression
  • War and genocide

Applicants can explore these issues from local, regional, national, or international perspectives.

4. Building Inclusive Societies

This theme focuses on social change and efforts to create societies in which more people can participate and thrive.

Potential areas include:

  • Youth-led peace movements
  • International solidarity
  • Climate justice
  • Healthcare
  • Education
  • Mental health among young people
  • Anxiety and depression
  • The relationship between social media and mental wellbeing
  • The cost of living and its effects on health
  • Poverty and physical wellbeing
  • Maternal mortality
  • Women’s and girls’ rights
  • Reproductive health
  • Caring for ageing parents
  • The economic pressures faced by families caring for multiple generations

The fellowship encourages applicants to approach these issues through the experiences of real people and communities.

5. Finding What Sustains Us

Not every important story is about conflict or crisis.

This theme focuses on the things that give people meaning, strengthen communities, preserve culture, and help people navigate difficult times.

Possible topics include:

  • Indigenous voices
  • Cultural identity
  • Second-generation immigrants
  • Belonging and identity
  • Diaspora experiences
  • Maintaining culture across borders
  • Sports as a tool for bringing people together
  • Music and art as tools for social connection
  • Pop culture and resistance
  • Fandoms
  • Cultural belonging
  • The politics of who gets to belong

This theme provides an opportunity for storytellers to explore the positive, creative, and cultural forces that connect people.

Fellowship Timeline

The One Humanity Fellowship follows a clear application and selection timeline.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).

Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

APPLY HERE

For more information about this fellowship programs, visit One Humanity Fellowship

Hop onto the OFY Website HERE for more fellowship opportunities

Fellowship Announcement

Accepted fellows are expected to be announced during the second week of September 2026.

Fellowship Commencement

The fellowship is scheduled to begin in October 2026.

The program will run for approximately three months.

Publication Schedule

During the fellowship, participants are expected to publish at least five pieces.

The pieces will be published on a biweekly schedule, meaning fellows must be prepared to consistently develop and submit work throughout the program.

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Emerging Storytellers

The One Humanity Fellowship combines several elements that can be particularly valuable for individuals seeking to develop a career in writing, journalism, advocacy, communications, media, research, or multimedia storytelling.

Rather than offering only financial support, the program combines:

  1. Publication opportunities
  2. Editorial mentorship
  3. Expert mentorship
  4. International exposure
  5. A professional cohort
  6. Potential speaking opportunities
  7. A $500 stipend
  8. Opportunities to develop a distinctive storytelling voice

The combination of these benefits can help emerging storytellers strengthen both their portfolio and professional network.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The fellowship is designed for emerging writers and multimedia producers at any career stage.

Applicants do not need a journalism degree or formal journalism training.

The organization particularly encourages applications from underrepresented regions and communities, especially individuals whose stories and perspectives are rarely represented in international media.

Geographic Eligibility

The information provided for the fellowship does not specify a restricted list of eligible countries or a particular continent.

Instead, WAOH states that it actively seeks applicants from underrepresented regions and communities around the world.

Therefore, the opportunity appears to have an international scope rather than being limited to applicants from a specific country or geographic region.

Applicants should nevertheless review the official application instructions carefully for any additional eligibility requirements before submitting their application.

Race, Ethnicity and Nationality

The fellowship description does not state that applicants must belong to a particular race, ethnicity, nationality, or continent.

Its emphasis is instead on supporting storytellers from underrepresented regions and communities and individuals whose stories rarely reach international media.

What Makes a Strong Applicant?

Although the fellowship is open to storytellers at any career stage, applicants should consider how clearly their application demonstrates the qualities WAOH is looking for.

A strong applicant would ideally be able to demonstrate:

  • A clear and distinctive voice
  • Genuine interest in human rights or civic life
  • Strong storytelling ability
  • A compelling perspective or lived experience
  • An understanding of an important issue affecting a community
  • The ability to develop original content
  • Commitment to meeting regular deadlines
  • Willingness to work collaboratively with editors
  • Interest in contributing to conversations that extend beyond their immediate community

Applicants should avoid simply describing an interest in human rights without demonstrating what they can contribute to the conversation.

Examples of Potential Story Ideas

The fellowship’s thematic areas provide significant room for creativity.

For example, an applicant from an African country could explore how young people are responding to political or economic challenges in their community.

A multimedia storyteller could create a short-form video series documenting how climate change is affecting a vulnerable community.

A writer could produce a personal essay about identity, migration, belonging, or cultural preservation.

A journalist could investigate an underreported human rights issue.

A photographer could develop a photo essay highlighting a community whose experiences receive little international attention.

A social media storyteller could examine how young people use digital platforms to organize, advocate, communicate, or build communities.

The important factor is not simply the topic but the perspective, originality, relevance, and storytelling approach.

Commitment Expected From Fellows

Applicants should understand that this is an active three-month fellowship rather than a one-time publication opportunity.

Selected fellows are expected to:

  • Participate throughout the three-month program
  • Work with editors
  • Develop original content
  • Publish at least five pieces
  • Follow a biweekly publication schedule
  • Meet regular deadlines
  • Engage with the fellowship community
  • Participate in mentorship opportunities
  • Contribute meaningfully to the program

Applicants should therefore only apply if they can realistically commit the necessary time and effort.

Application Deadline and Important Dates

For quick reference, the key dates are:

  • Application deadline: August 21, 2026
  • Deadline time: 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT)
  • Selected fellows announced: Second week of September 2026
  • Fellowship begins: October 2026
  • Program duration: Three months
  • Expected publications: At least five pieces
  • Publication frequency: Biweekly

Applicants should pay particular attention to the time zone when calculating the deadline.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should submit their application through the official One Humanity Fellowship application process.

Before applying, prospective fellows should carefully review the fellowship requirements and consider:

  • Which thematic area best fits their interests
  • What unique perspective they can bring
  • Which storytelling format best communicates their idea
  • What stories or issues they want to explore
  • Whether they can commit to the full three-month program
  • Whether they can meet the biweekly publication schedule

Applicants should also ensure that their submission clearly communicates their voice, interests, and motivation for joining the fellowship.

Important Information for Applicants

The One Humanity Fellowship is intended for people who have something meaningful to say and want support in saying it.

It is not simply a platform for obtaining a publication credit.

The program is structured around a genuine relationship between fellows and editors, meaning applicants should be prepared to receive feedback, revise their work, develop ideas, and collaborate throughout the fellowship.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to people who want to grow as storytellers rather than simply add another credential to their CV.

Conclusion

The One Humanity Fellowship 2026 presents an opportunity for emerging writers and multimedia producers to develop original stories, receive professional editorial and expert mentorship, build international connections, and have their work published to a global audience.

With opportunities spanning journalism, analytical writing, personal essays, photography, video, audio, and social media storytelling, the fellowship is designed to accommodate different forms of creative and journalistic expression.

The program’s five thematic areas — Responding to Threats Against Democracy, Moving Beyond Polarization, Fighting for Human Rights, Building Inclusive Societies, and Finding What Sustains Us — give applicants a broad platform to explore important issues affecting people and communities around the world.

Another significant advantage is that applicants do not need a journalism degree or formal journalism training. What matters is a genuine engagement with human rights or civic issues, a distinct voice or perspective, and the willingness to commit to the fellowship’s requirements.

Selected fellows will receive editorial mentorship, expert mentorship, publication opportunities, potential webinar speaking opportunities, access to an international cohort community, and a $500 stipend for their time and work.

The application deadline is August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT). Successful applicants are expected to be announced during the second week of September, with the fellowship beginning in October 2026.

For writers, journalists, content creators, photographers, filmmakers, audio storytellers, and other emerging multimedia producers who have an important story to tell, the One Humanity Fellowship could provide the editorial support, platform, network, and resources needed to take that story to a wider audience.

Interested applicants are encouraged to apply before the deadline and carefully demonstrate the unique perspective, community, issue, or story they would bring to the One Humanity Fellowship.

item.content:encoded:
Victoria University (VU) in Melbourne, Australia, is accepting applications for its Research Period 1 intake for students interested in undertaking higher degree by research programs. The opportunity provides prospective researchers with a pathway to pursue advanced research through master’s by research, PhD, and integrated research programs at one of Australia’s major universities.

Applicants interested in joining Victoria University as research students must follow a structured application process that includes identifying an appropriate research area, finding a prospective supervisor, preparing a research proposal, demonstrating academic eligibility, and submitting the required supporting documentation.

For international applicants, the opportunity also provides a potential pathway to undertake postgraduate research in Australia, subject to meeting Victoria University’s academic, English-language, visa, and other admission requirements.

Victoria University Research Degrees 2027

Victoria University offers research opportunities for candidates who want to develop advanced expertise through independent research. Research students work with academic supervisors to investigate a defined research problem and contribute to knowledge within their chosen discipline.

The university’s research environment places particular emphasis on research addressing the health of the environment and communities. Its research agenda also includes work connected to Indigenous communities, social justice, decolonisation, climate change, identity, displacement, and international activist connections.

Research candidates may be able to undertake their research with an industry partner through the VU INSPIRED program, providing an opportunity to connect academic research with practical industry challenges.

Research Period 1 Is Now Open

Victoria University has opened applications for Research Period 1.

The application process and deadlines depend on whether an applicant is classified as a domestic or international applicant. Prospective students should therefore check the applicable application dates before preparing and submitting their application.

Applicants who receive an offer and accept their place must be available to present in Melbourne by the specified enrolment date.

International applicants should pay particular attention to the distinction between offshore and onshore applications, as different deadlines may apply.

What Research Degrees Can Applicants Pursue?

The Victoria University research pathway includes different levels of higher degree research study.

Applicants should first determine which research study level is appropriate for their academic background and research ambitions.

Depending on the relevant course and eligibility requirements, applicants may pursue research through:

  • Master’s research degrees
  • PhD programs
  • PhD (Integrated) programs
  • Higher degree by research pathways
  • Admission with advanced candidature for eligible students transferring from another higher education institution

The appropriate course depends on the applicant’s previous qualifications, research experience, proposed research topic, and the research area available at Victoria University.

How to Apply for a Victoria University Research Degree

The university outlines a structured process for prospective research students.

Step 1: Select a Suitable Study Level

Step 2: Check Your Eligibility

Step 3: Find a Research Focus Outline

Step 4: Identify a Priority Field of Research and Supervisor

Step 5: Prepare Your Research Proposal

Step 6: Submit Your Application

Once the required documents have been prepared and the prospective supervisor has provided the required approval, applicants can submit their application through the appropriate application pathway.

The application process differs between domestic and international applicants.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants will need to prepare several supporting documents.

The required application materials include:

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide their academic transcripts as part of the application.

These documents allow Victoria University to assess the applicant’s previous academic performance and qualifications.

Qualification Certificates

Applicants must also provide evidence of their completed academic qualifications.

This may include relevant degree certificates or other official qualification documentation.

Research Proposal

The research proposal is required and should include the relevant research information, including:

  • Proposed research topic
  • Supervisor’s name
  • Research Focus Outline
  • Priority Field of Research

The proposal should demonstrate a clear connection between the applicant’s proposed research and the university’s available research areas.

200-Word Personal Statement

Applicants must submit a 200-word personal statement.

The statement should explain:

  • Why the applicant wants to undertake the proposed research
  • Their reasons for choosing the research area
  • Their academic pathway or trajectory

Although the statement is short, applicants should use the available space effectively to demonstrate their motivation and academic direction.

Updated CV

Applicants need to provide an up-to-date curriculum vitae.

The CV should provide relevant information about the applicant’s academic background, research experience, professional experience, publications, projects, achievements, and other relevant qualifications where applicable.

Signed HDR Prospective Supervisor Form

Applicants must provide the signed HDR prospective supervisor form confirming that they have sought and received in-principle supervision support.

This document is a required component of the application.

Applications should therefore not be submitted without completing this requirement.

Domestic Applicants

Victoria University defines domestic applicants as:

  • Australian citizens
  • Australian permanent residents
  • New Zealand citizens

Domestic applicants should begin by selecting an appropriate research degree and reviewing the corresponding course page.

If the course is currently open for applications, an Apply button will be available on the course page.

If an Apply button is not available, prospective applicants can use the university’s enquiry process to express their interest and request notification when applications reopen.

Research Training Program for Domestic Applicants

Domestic applicants will be considered for an Australian government-funded place under the Research Training Program (RTP).

However, applicants should be aware that funding applies only for the relevant funded period.

If a student’s enrolment continues beyond the funded period of support, they may become liable for tuition fees at the applicable yearly rate per semester of enrolment.

Successful domestic applicants will receive a formal offer by email from Victoria University’s Admissions team.

International Applicants

International applicants follow a different application pathway.

International candidates must submit their applications through Victoria University International.

Applicants need to select a thesis unit assigned to the relevant research course.

The process generally requires prospective international students to:

  • Select the appropriate research degree
  • Identify the relevant institute
  • Select the international student option on the course page
  • Review the course structure and available units
  • Select the appropriate thesis unit
  • Complete the required application
  • Submit the required supporting documents

Successful international applicants will receive a formal Letter of Offer from VU International.

International applicants should carefully check the relevant deadlines for both offshore and onshore applications before submitting their applications.

Admission With Advanced Candidature

Victoria University also provides a pathway for certain applicants who are already enrolled in a higher degree by research at another institution.

If you are currently undertaking a higher degree by research elsewhere and want to transfer to Victoria University, you may be eligible for admission with advanced candidature.

However, additional documentation is required.

Applicants must submit an Advanced Candidature Supervisor Form completed by their prospective supervisor.

The university states that applications will not be considered if the required advanced candidature documentation is incomplete or missing from the application.

This pathway can therefore be particularly relevant to existing research students seeking to continue their research at Victoria University.

Enrolment and Commencement

Applicants who receive an offer and accept a place should carefully review their enrolment and commencement requirements.

The enrolment date depends on the specific research degree.

Students must be prepared to present in Melbourne by the specified enrolment date once their place has been accepted.

This is particularly important for international students who may need to make arrangements involving:

  • Australian visa requirements
  • International travel
  • Accommodation
  • Arrival in Melbourne
  • University enrolment
  • Orientation
  • Research preparation

Applicants should therefore plan their relocation and arrival well in advance of the required commencement date.

Research Preparatory Coursework

New research students may be required to complete compulsory research preparatory coursework units associated with their degree.

This requirement applies unless the student has received approved Advanced Standing before enrolment.

The coursework requirements differ according to the type of research degree.

Master’s Degrees and PhD (Integrated)

For Research Period 1, 2027, research preparatory coursework for master’s degrees and PhD (Integrated) programs is scheduled to begin on:

15 February 2027

The preparatory coursework is delivered in person at Victoria University’s Footscray Park Campus in Melbourne.

Classes are normally held during business hours.

Students should therefore take the in-person nature of these preparatory units into consideration when planning their arrival and accommodation.

PhD Programs

For PhD students enrolling on 15 February 2027, the Research Period 1 coursework begins on:

5 March 2027

Students enrolling after this date will follow the relevant coursework arrangements for Research Period 1, 2027.

Victoria University also provides a multi-entry intake arrangement for domestic PhD students.

PhD Coursework Delivery

The PhD preparatory units use a hybrid delivery model designed to provide greater flexibility.

The program includes:

  • Online real-time classes
  • On-campus learning
  • A Saturday intensive at Footscray Park Campus
  • An on-campus PhD coursework conference

The coursework units therefore combine online learning with face-to-face academic activities.

Students should be prepared to participate in both online and on-campus components.

Research With Industry Partners Through VU INSPIRED

Students may also have the opportunity to conduct research in collaboration with an industry partner through Victoria University’s VU INSPIRED program.

This can provide a bridge between academic research and real-world industry applications.

Industry-linked research can be valuable for students who want their research to have practical applications beyond academia.

It may also help researchers develop experience working with organisations outside the university environment.

Important Dates for Research Period 1, 2027

Applicants should pay close attention to the relevant application and enrolment dates because deadlines can differ depending on applicant status and study level.

Key dates provided for Research Period 1, 2027 include:

Research Activity Date
Research Period 1 2027
Master’s & PhD (Integrated) preparatory coursework 15 February 2027
PhD coursework for students enrolling 15 February 5 March 2027
Application deadline Depends on domestic/international status and applicable intake
Enrolment date Depends on the accepted research degree

International applicants should specifically check the applicable onshore and offshore deadlines before submitting an application

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity may be particularly suitable for students and researchers who want to pursue advanced research in Australia and whose proposed research aligns with Victoria University’s available research expertise.

Potential applicants include:

  • Graduates seeking master’s-level research study
  • Students interested in doctoral research
  • Candidates pursuing a PhD (Integrated)
  • Existing higher degree research students seeking transfer through advanced candidature
  • Researchers interested in community and environmental health
  • Applicants interested in Indigenous research
  • Researchers interested in social justice
  • Candidates researching climate change
  • Researchers exploring displacement and identity
  • Applicants interested in self-determination and community empowerment
  • Candidates interested in international activist connections
  • Researchers seeking industry-connected research opportunities

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Final Thoughts

Victoria University’s Research Period 1, 2027 intake provides prospective research students with an opportunity to pursue advanced research in Melbourne while working within an established academic research environment.

The application process requires considerably more preparation than a standard coursework degree application. Prospective candidates must identify a suitable research area, find an appropriate supervisor, obtain in-principle supervisory approval, prepare a research proposal, identify the relevant Field of Research code, and compile the required academic and personal documents.

For international applicants, additional planning is particularly important because the application pathway, deadlines, international admission process, visa requirements, and Melbourne commencement arrangements must all be considered.

Applicants should begin preparing well before their applicable deadline, particularly because securing a prospective supervisor and developing a strong research proposal can take time.

The most important point for prospective candidates is to check the applicable Research Period 1 deadline based on their domestic or international status and ensure that the required supervisor approval and documentation are completed before submitting the application

 

Click HERE for Research opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Journalists in Residence Program 2027 at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. The program offers an intensive 12-week learning and professional development experience for journalists from around the world who want to deepen their understanding of the relationship between politics, business, markets, and economic power.

Hosted by the Stigler Center for the Study of the Economy and the State at the University of Chicago, the program brings together a small international cohort of journalists for an immersive experience on the Hyde Park campus.

Participants will study alongside faculty and students, audit graduate-level business courses, participate in Stigler Center seminars and events, and explore how economic and political forces influence the companies, markets, and institutions they cover.

About the Journalists in Residence Program

The Journalists in Residence Program is designed for journalists interested in gaining a deeper understanding of the interactions between politics and the economy.

During the 12-week residency, participants will become part of an international cohort and engage with the academic environment at the University of Chicago. Journalists will have the opportunity to audit three graduate-level business courses at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.

Participants will also attend weekly Stigler Center seminars and events, giving them opportunities to engage with researchers, faculty, and other members of the academic community.

The program is particularly relevant for journalists who cover business, economics, markets, political economy, regulation, corporations, and concentrated economic power.

What Will Participants Do?

During the residency, journalists will:

  • Audit three graduate-level business courses at Chicago Booth.
  • Attend weekly Stigler Center seminars and events.
  • Study alongside University of Chicago faculty and students.
  • Develop a deeper understanding of business and economic decision-making.
  • Examine how managers make decisions.
  • Explore the role of boards, courts, regulators, and the profit motive.
  • Gain perspectives that can contribute to stronger and more informed journalism.
  • Engage with an international community of journalists and academics.

The program provides journalists with an opportunity to step away from their normal reporting environment and develop new perspectives that can strengthen their coverage of economic and political issues.

Financial Support

Selected participants receive financial support during the residency.

The program provides:

  • A living stipend
  • Reimbursement for round-trip airfare
  • Reimbursement for visa fees

The program therefore provides substantial support to help selected journalists participate in the residency in Chicago.

Who Can Apply?

The program is intended for journalists from around the world who are interested in deepening their understanding of the relationship between politics and the economy.

Applicants should have:

  • Several years of journalism experience.
  • An interest in political economy, business, markets, or related areas.
  • Proficient English-language skills.
  • A demonstrated record of journalism through published work.

The program is particularly suited to journalists who report on business and markets and want to strengthen their understanding of the economic and institutional forces behind the stories they cover.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit the following materials through the online application system:

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants should provide a current CV highlighting their professional and journalism experience.

2. Personal Statements

Applicants must submit personal statements explaining their interest in the program and their goals for participating in the residency.

3. Two Letters of Recommendation

Two letters of recommendation are required.

The recommenders must submit their letters directly through the separate recommendation portal. Applicants cannot submit letters on behalf of their recommenders.

4. Three Published News Articles

Applicants must provide three published news articles demonstrating their journalism experience.

For articles that were not originally published in English, applicants should provide an English translation alongside the original articles.

TV and radio journalists may provide links to their video or audio work in a PDF or Word document together with English transcriptions.

5. Proof of English Proficiency

Non-native English speakers may be required to provide proof of English proficiency.

Acceptable evidence can include standardized test scores or certificates such as TOEFL, IELTS, SAT, ACT, Cambridge, or Duolingo. Other forms of evidence, including education or professional experience in an English-speaking environment, may also be accepted.

Application Process

All application materials must be submitted through the online application portal.

Materials sent by email, social media, or other methods will not be considered.

Applicants should prepare their CV, personal statements, recommendation arrangements, published articles, and any required English-language documentation before submitting the application.

Important Dates

Application Deadline: September 20, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CT Chicago time

Selection Decisions: Expected by the end of December 2026

Program Dates: March 15 – May 31, 2027

Why Apply?

The University of Chicago Journalists in Residence Program offers journalists an opportunity to combine professional journalism experience with advanced academic learning.

Through access to graduate-level business courses, seminars, faculty, and researchers, participants can develop a stronger understanding of the economic and political systems behind the issues they report on.

For journalists covering business, markets, corporations, regulation, economic policy, or political economy, the residency can provide valuable knowledge and perspectives that can inform future reporting.

How to Apply

Interested journalists should prepare all required application materials and submit them through the official online application portal before the deadline.

Application Deadline: September 20, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CT

Program: March 15 – May 31, 2027

Location: University of Chicago Booth School of Business, Hyde Park, Chicago, USA

Apply Now: University of Chicago Journalists in Residence Program Application

For questions about the application, applicants can contact the Stigler Center at stiglercenter@chicagobooth.edu.

Conclusion

The University of Chicago Journalists in Residence Program 2027 is an opportunity for experienced journalists to deepen their understanding of business, markets, political economy, and economic power while studying within one of the world’s leading academic environments.

If you are a journalist with several years of experience and a strong interest in how politics and economics shape the institutions and markets you cover, consider preparing your application early and submitting it before September 20, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Eric Bleumink Scholarship 2027 offers an exciting opportunity for talented international students to pursue an eligible Master’s degree at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands.

The scholarship is intended for academically outstanding students and provides financial support toward major costs associated with studying abroad. It is an excellent opportunity for students seeking a fully funded Master’s opportunity in Europe and looking to study at an internationally recognised research university.

About the Eric Bleumink Scholarship

The Eric Bleumink Scholarship provides talented students from around the world with the opportunity to undertake postgraduate studies at the University of Groningen.

The scholarship is particularly valuable for international students who have strong academic records and require financial support to pursue their studies.

Selected students can benefit from financial assistance covering several important costs, allowing them to concentrate on their academic development and make the most of their experience in the Netherlands.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The Eric Bleumink Scholarship offers extensive financial support. According to the provided opportunity information, the benefits include:

  • Full tuition fee coverage
  • International travel expenses
  • Living expenses
  • Health insurance
  • Books and study materials
  • Financial support for academic expenses
  • The opportunity to study at a leading European research university
  • Access to an international academic environment and network

These benefits can substantially reduce the financial challenges associated with pursuing a Master’s degree abroad.

Available Master’s Programmes

The scholarship is available for eligible Master’s programmes offered by the University of Groningen.

Potential areas of study include:

Arts and Humanities

Students interested in humanities, culture, languages, history, and related disciplines may find eligible programmes within this broad field.

Business and Economics

The university offers opportunities for students interested in business, economics, management, and related areas.

Law

Students interested in legal studies can explore eligible Master’s programmes in law and related disciplines.

Science and Engineering

The opportunity also covers eligible programmes within science, technology, engineering, and related fields.

Social Sciences

Students interested in society, politics, development, international relations, and related disciplines can explore relevant programmes.

Medical and Health Sciences

Eligible programmes may also be available in medical and health-related fields.

Environmental Sciences

Students interested in environmental issues, sustainability, climate, and related areas can explore eligible programmes.

Information Technology

Applicants interested in technology, computing, and information systems may also find eligible Master’s programmes.

Education

Eligible graduate programmes in education and related areas are also included.

Important: Applicants should verify that their chosen Master’s programme is eligible and meets the specific admission requirements of the University of Groningen.

Who Is Eligible?

The scholarship is intended for international students applying for eligible Master’s programmes at the University of Groningen.

Applicants should generally:

  • Be an international student.
  • Apply for an eligible Master’s programme at the University of Groningen.
  • Have an outstanding academic record.
  • Demonstrate financial need.
  • Meet the university’s English-language requirements.
  • Provide strong academic or professional recommendations where required.
  • Meet the admission requirements of their selected Master’s programme.
  • Be committed to successfully completing the programme.

Because Master’s programmes can have different requirements, applicants should carefully check the conditions attached to their specific programme.

Academic Excellence

Academic performance is an important consideration for this opportunity. Prospective applicants should ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate their ability to succeed in postgraduate study.

A strong academic profile, together with a well-prepared admission application, can help applicants present themselves competitively.

English Language Requirements

Applicants must meet the English-language requirements associated with their chosen Master’s programme.

Depending on the programme, applicants may be required to provide evidence of English proficiency through an accepted language test or another recognised form of evidence.

Students should check the requirements of their specific programme before submitting their application.

Documents to Prepare

Applicants should prepare the documents required for admission to their selected Master’s programme. These may include:

  • Academic transcripts
  • Degree certificates
  • Curriculum vitae (CV)
  • Motivation letter or personal statement
  • Recommendation letters
  • Valid passport or national identification document
  • English-language proficiency certificate
  • Proof of financial circumstances, where required
  • Other programme-specific documents

Applicants should ensure that all documents are accurate, complete, and prepared according to the university’s instructions.

How the Scholarship Application Works

One important feature of the Eric Bleumink Scholarship is that there is no separate scholarship application according to the information provided.

Instead, eligible candidates are considered for nomination through the Master’s admission process.

Step 1: Choose a Master’s Programme

First, identify an eligible Master’s programme at the University of Groningen that matches your academic background and career goals.

Step 2: Check the Admission Requirements

Carefully review the programme’s academic, language, and documentation requirements.

Step 3: Prepare Your Documents

Gather your transcripts, degree certificates, CV, motivation statement, recommendations, and other required documents.

Step 4: Submit Your Master’s Application

Complete and submit your application for admission to the University of Groningen before the relevant deadline.

Step 5: Scholarship Consideration

Eligible and outstanding candidates may be nominated by the university for the Eric Bleumink Scholarship.

This means applicants should focus on submitting a strong and complete Master’s admission application.

Why Study in the Netherlands?

Studying in the Netherlands can provide international students with an opportunity to experience a highly international academic environment while gaining advanced knowledge and skills.

The country is home to internationally recognised universities and offers a diverse learning environment that brings together students and researchers from different parts of the world.

For students interested in building an international academic and professional network, studying in the Netherlands can be a valuable experience.

Why Choose the University of Groningen?

The University of Groningen is one of the Netherlands’ longstanding research universities and offers a broad selection of Master’s programmes.

Students have the opportunity to study in an international academic environment while engaging with research, innovation, and interdisciplinary learning.

The university’s international community can also provide students with opportunities to build connections with peers and academics from different countries and academic backgrounds.

Application Timeline

Prospective applicants should pay close attention to the application timeline.

Master’s application deadline for consideration:
📅 December 1, 2026

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing their applications early. Waiting until the final days can create unnecessary pressure, particularly if academic documents, recommendation letters, language test results, or other supporting materials are required.

Important Note for Applicants

The scholarship information provided states that eligible candidates are considered for the fellowship after applying for admission and that there is no separate scholarship application.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that submitting a general scholarship form is necessary. Instead, they should carefully follow the University of Groningen’s Master’s admission process and confirm the latest requirements for their selected programme.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Eric Bleumink Scholarship fully funded?

The provided scholarship information describes the opportunity as fully funded and lists support for tuition, international travel, living expenses, health insurance, books, and study materials.

Who can apply?

The opportunity is aimed at international students seeking admission to eligible Master’s programmes at the University of Groningen.

Is there a separate scholarship application?

No. According to the provided information, eligible candidates are considered for nomination after applying for admission to an eligible Master’s programme.

What level of study is supported?

The scholarship supports eligible Master’s degree programmes.

Which subjects are available?

Eligible programmes span areas such as Arts and Humanities, Business and Economics, Law, Science, Engineering, Social Sciences, Medical Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Information Technology, Education, and other eligible graduate programmes.

When is the deadline?

The application deadline stated in the provided information is December 1, 2026.

Where is the scholarship located?

The scholarship is hosted by the University of Groningen in the Netherlands.

Conclusion

The Eric Bleumink Scholarship 2027 is a valuable opportunity for academically strong international students who want to pursue a Master’s degree in the Netherlands without carrying the full financial burden of international study.

Beyond financial support, the opportunity can provide students with access to an international academic environment, research opportunities, and a diverse network of students and scholars.

If you are considering postgraduate study in Europe, this is an opportunity worth exploring. Start by identifying an eligible Master’s programme, reviewing its admission requirements, preparing your supporting documents, and submitting your application well before the December 1, 2026 deadline.
